Reading the wireframe

Teal marks anything the child controls. Red handwriting is a design note, not screen copy. Everything else is structure.

THE CHILD'S SIDE — left to right, the order a child meets it.

The channel only opens when they hold the button, and every screen after that is a decision they make: who hears it, whether to send it at all, what gets passed on tonight.

WHAT THE ADULTS RECEIVE — deliberately less than they want.

Two sentences, one voice note, and a page stating the limits. Gran gets her own inbox rather than a view of anyone else's.

OPEN, NOT DRAWN

· What the child sees when a parent never replies — the failure mode that matters most and has no screen yet.

· Whether topic extraction runs on the voluntary note only. If so there is no ambient mic anywhere in the product, and the COPPA question in the brief mostly dissolves.
